confirmed.statement: The first slice enables an authorised service agent to create one valid synthetic service request in a model-driven app and observe its saved status.
confirmed.basis: The exact case input supplies the outcome, persona, host, required fields, and feedback requirement.

confirmed.statement: One solution-owned Dataverse service-request table and the platform save path are the only persistence owner for this slice.
confirmed.basis: The exact case input requires one table, no integration, and no AI.

assumptions.statement: Environment-specific publisher prefix, role binding, telemetry destination, and retention values will be configured before authorised implementation.
assumptions.impact: These values affect deployment configuration but do not change the bounded architecture or security model.
assumptions.validation_required: An authorised implementer must record the values and configuration readback before deployment approval.

rejected.decision: Add unrelated tables, flows, integrations, AI features, or a second custom write path.
rejected.reason: They are unnecessary for the first observable end-to-end outcome and would create a horizontal or duplicate-owner design.
rejected.reconsider_if: A later approved slice has a distinct measurable outcome that requires one of those components.

slice.outcome: An authorised service agent creates one valid synthetic request with title, category, and priority in the model-driven app and can observe the persisted status and correlation reference.
scope: Model-driven create form for one synthetic service-request table
Required-field, permission, duplicate, and concurrency controls
User feedback, privacy-safe telemetry, deployment evidence, and rollback
exclusions: Additional tables or custom persistence handlers
Tenant access, implementation, deployment, or runtime claims
slice.entry: An authenticated service agent with the least-privilege create role opens the model-driven app create form and initiates a new request.
slice.validation: Before save, require title, category, and priority; confirm create privilege and permitted owner; validate allowed values; bind a client submission key; and reject missing, invalid, duplicate, or stale/concurrent submissions without overwriting either version.
slice.persistence_or_action: The model-driven platform save path writes once to the solution-owned service-request table as the sole write owner. The submission key prevents duplicate create actions, and any later update must present the current version or concurrency token.
slice.feedback: Show loading and disabled-submit states, a success confirmation with saved status and correlation reference, field-level validation errors, a permission-safe denial, a duplicate outcome, and a stale/conflict message that instructs the agent to reload and reconcile; transient failure permits a safe retry with the same submission key.
slice.telemetry: Emit privacy-safe create-started, create-succeeded, validation-failed, permission-denied, duplicate-detected, conflict-detected, and create-failed events with correlation ID, outcome, duration, and synthetic record reference; exclude title and business payload; assign an operational owner and retention policy before deployment.
slice.evidence: Keep static schema/form/role review, automated validation and concurrency tests, solution artifact integrity, target import/configuration readback, and runtime create/failure/replay proof as separate evidence levels; none of the latter three is claimed by this brief.

experience.decision: Use the model-driven main form with required indicators, accessible error summary, disabled duplicate submit, success confirmation, and conflict recovery guidance.
experience.rationale: It completes the supplied operator journey and exposes every required state.

data.decision: Use one solution-owned service-request table with title, category, priority, status, submission key, owner, and platform concurrency metadata.
data.rationale: One authoritative table and platform save path meet the outcome while preventing duplicate write ownership.

integration.decision: Use no integration component in this slice.
integration.rationale: The outcome is completed entirely through the model-driven platform save path.

ai.decision: Use no AI component in this slice.
ai.rationale: The exact input excludes AI and all validation is deterministic.

security.decision: Grant only the service-request create/read privileges and permitted ownership scope; deny save before persistence when authorization fails.
security.rationale: Least privilege and a safe permission-failure contract are required by the slice.

operations.decision: Monitor privacy-safe outcome events by correlation ID and alert on sustained create failures, permission anomalies, duplicate spikes, or conflicts.
operations.rationale: The operator needs diagnosable failure and replay evidence without capturing payload content.

alm.decision: Package the table, form, app, role changes, and configuration references in one solution; use unmanaged Dev and an approved managed downstream path with preflight, post-import readback, and rollback to the prior managed version.
alm.rationale: This is the minimum promotable slice and keeps deployment authorization separate from brief readiness.

acceptance_criteria.given: An authorised service agent and valid synthetic title, category, and priority
acceptance_criteria.when: the agent submits the create form once
acceptance_criteria.then: one request is saved and the app shows its persisted status and correlation reference
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Runtime create trace plus Dataverse readback in an authorised target environment

acceptance_criteria.given: A required or allowed-value validation failure
acceptance_criteria.then: no request is saved and accessible field-level feedback identifies the correction
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Automated form validation result and runtime no-write proof

acceptance_criteria.then: persistence is denied without exposing restricted details and a permission event is correlated
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Role matrix, negative authorization test, and privacy-safe telemetry

acceptance_criteria.given: A duplicate submission key or a stale concurrency token
acceptance_criteria.when: the save or later overwrite is attempted
acceptance_criteria.then: no duplicate or stale overwrite occurs and the user is told to reuse the existing result or reload and reconcile
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Concurrent-change and duplicate-submission tests with record-count and version evidence

acceptance_criteria.given: The managed slice is approved for target import
acceptance_criteria.then: the app, form, table, privileges, and telemetry references match the approved package before runtime testing begins
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Import log, solution component inventory, configuration readback, and approval record

negative_paths.condition: Title, category, or priority is missing or invalid.
negative_paths.expected_behavior: Block save, retain safe input, identify invalid fields, and emit validation-failed telemetry without payload values.

negative_paths.condition: The actor lacks create or ownership permission.
negative_paths.expected_behavior: Deny persistence, show a safe permission message, and emit a correlated denial event.

negative_paths.condition: The same submission is replayed or an update uses stale state.
negative_paths.expected_behavior: Prevent duplicate action or overwrite, preserve both versions, and instruct reload and reconciliation.

negative_paths.condition: A transient save or telemetry failure occurs.
negative_paths.expected_behavior: Show failure without false success; allow an idempotent retry and make telemetry delivery failure observable.

tests.scope: Valid create, required-field validation, allowed values, success, and failure feedback
tests.expected: Exactly one valid request is saved and invalid requests produce no write.
tests.evidence_required: Automated test results and authorised runtime trace

tests.expected: Authorised actors succeed and unauthorised actors receive a safe denial with no write.
tests.evidence_required: Role configuration readback and positive/negative runtime tests

tests.scope: Duplicate submission, retry, and stale/concurrent save handling
tests.expected: Only one create occurs, stale overwrite is rejected, and retry is idempotent.
tests.evidence_required: Record count, version evidence, telemetry correlation, and user feedback capture

tests.scope: Required indicators, focus, error summary, and status announcements
tests.expected: Keyboard and assistive-technology users can identify and recover from every form state.
Imported components and bindings match the approved package before enablement.
tests.evidence_required: Deployment log, import result, inventory, and readback

tests.scope: Rollback to the prior managed version and preservation of created records
tests.expected: The prior app version is restored and data disposition follows the approved rollback decision.
tests.evidence_required: Rollback execution record, solution version readback, and data reconciliation

prerequisites: Approved publisher, solution owner, table logical names, role mapping, DLP classification, telemetry destination, retention, and support owner
Managed downstream deployment path and rollback version are approved
No tenant credential or target access is provided to this reasoning-only workflow
steps: Implement and test the smallest solution-owned table, form, app, role, and telemetry configuration in authorised Dev
Export the approved managed artifact and validate component inventory and dependencies
Import through the authorised downstream process without activating unverified integrations
Perform configuration readback before runtime testing
post_deploy_checks: Verify table, columns, form, app, role privilege depth, and configuration references
Run happy, validation, permission, duplicate, conflict, telemetry, and retry smoke tests
Confirm support ownership and alert routing
evidence_required: Managed solution hash and component inventory

triggers: Duplicate writes, unrecoverable save failure, or unacceptable conflict behavior
steps: Disable access to the new app slice and preserve correlation evidence
Restore the prior approved managed solution version through the authorised process
Re-read configuration and rerun the prior-version smoke test
Reconcile records created during the change window
data_considerations: Do not delete created requests automatically
Preserve audit and correlation evidence under the approved retention policy
Document any schema rollback constraint before import
rollback.owner: Authorised solution owner with platform operations

next_action: Authorised solution owner approves the bounded Dev configuration values and hands this Ready brief to implementation; carry forward only this first-slice decision, its exclusions, and the still-unexecuted deployment/runtime evidence plan.
